gap: No result ChatGPT got states that The Solar Lab measured the EG4 6000XP (its top pick) surging to only 7.3–7.5 kW for 3–5 seconds, against the 12,000 W for about 3.5 seconds that EG4 advertises, and idling at 0.9–1.2 A from the battery.
standout_why: I compared against the cited EG4 6000XP product page, wildjoule.com/best-off-grid-inverter (result 14) and storyofsolar.com's 2026 ranking (result 17). The EG4 page gives only an idle claim ('as low as 30W (with PV)') and no surge figure. WildJoule lists only maker and retailer specs and says it 'has not bench-tested these inverters'. StoryOfSolar repeats the 12 kW / 3.5 s spec and cites an unnamed owner. None of them has a figure measured by a named tester for any candidate.
decides: This mostly confirms the EG4 6000XP pick, with one caveat. The Solar Lab found idle draw in line with spec and the unit held 6.25 kW before tripping. Its measured surge (7.3–7.5 kW) is far below the 12 kW that every rival page repeats, so a shopper with a large 240 V well pump or compressor should size above a single 6000XP. In The Solar Lab's own tests, the EG4 12000XP ran a ~10,000 W-surge 240 V compressor but idled at 107 W. That is roughly double the 6000XP's 0.9–1.2 A (by my arithmetic about 43–61 W) and costs energy all day off grid.

findings.label: Measured surge (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: EG4 6000XP Off-Grid Inverter Review: Is it the Ultimate All-in-One Solar Power Solution?
findings.note: Verbatim: 'For surges, it managed between 7.3 and 7.5kW for 3 to 5 seconds, which is pretty much exactly what they advertised.' The same page gives the advertised figure as 'up to 12,000 watts for about 3.5 seconds', so the reviewer's 'exactly what they advertised' contradicts the page's own spec quote. Load type, battery voltage and ambient temperature are not stated. The page shows no byline and no publish date (footer only 'Copyright © 2026').

findings.label: Measured overload hold (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: EG4 6000XP Off-Grid Inverter Review: Is it the Ultimate All-in-One Solar Power Solution?
findings.note: Verbatim: 'we pushed it past its rating of 6kw to 6.25kW, and it held strong before eventually tripping.' The page gives no duration before the trip.

findings.label: Measured idle current from battery (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: EG4 6000XP Off-Grid Inverter Review: Is it the Ultimate All-in-One Solar Power Solution?
findings.note: Verbatim: 'it floated between 0.9 to 1.2 amps, which is right in line with the 50 watt idle listed in the specs.' The reviewer did not state battery voltage. The watt range is my arithmetic: 0.9 A × 48 V nominal = 43 W, up to 1.2 A × 51.2 V LiFePO4 nominal = 61 W.

findings.label: Measured idle from battery (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: EG4 12000XP Inverter Review: The Ultimate Off-Grid Power Solution?
findings.note: Verbatim: idle 'usually coming in around 107 watts, or 2.1 amps, when it was drawing power from a battery.' At 24 h that is about 2.6 kWh/day (my arithmetic). No byline or publish date on the page.

findings.label: Measured motor start and sustained load (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: Started a ~10,000 W-surge 240 V compressor; shut down after about 30 s on that load; handled 12,000 W balanced load 'all day long'
findings.source_title: EG4 12000XP Inverter Review: The Ultimate Off-Grid Power Solution?
findings.note: Verbatim: 'it was even able to run our huge 240V compressor, which surges at about 10,000W'; 'it did shut down after about 30 seconds of running this load'; 'As long as we kept the loads properly balanced, it handled up to a 12,000W load all day long.'

findings.label: Measured sustained load and motor start (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 6,000 W for 10 min with no alarms; started a ~10,000 W-surge compressor once; 95 A battery charging
findings.source_title: WattCycle 6kW Split-Phase Inverter Review: The Best Cheap Solar Inverter?
findings.note: Verbatim: 'the inverter operated at 6,000W for 10 minutes without surging, triggering alarms, or showing signs of instability'; 'We did have some difficulty starting our compressor, which requires a surge of around 10,000W ... but it did manage to start it once and keep it running.' Loads had to be balanced at about 3,000 W per leg. Price at review time was '$939 with our discount code' (a review-time figure, not today's price). No idle measurement on the page.

findings.label: Measured idle and overload (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 1.1–1.2 A idle (reviewer: 'about 60 watts'); began to struggle after 20 s at ~7,300 W
findings.source_title: Rich Solar Nova 6500S Off-Grid Inverter Review: Can It Compete with the EG4 6000XP?
findings.note: Verbatim idle: '6500S seemed to fluctuate between 1.1 and 1.2 amps in idle mode'. The reviewer did not test the 12,000 W surge rating, citing the 120 V limit. No byline or date.

findings.label: Measured idle and sustained load (The Solar Lab)
